solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Reckoned copper acted all strange when going outside

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go outside, wrapping round the chemical symbol
strange signals that the letters of acted all are rearranged into an odd order

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer is suspected of behaving oddly while out on the beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the metal; 'strange' makes CALLATED, and 'when going outside' wraps it round the symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past tenses of verbs for working out sums or estimating, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Conservative politician entertains a group of supporters

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so these letters take in the next piece

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A Tory MP hosts a party of loyal backers.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp is a faction or side whose members back the same cause, as in the rival camps of a party.

clue.text: Advanced slowly, not reaching the end

indicators.note: the musical term stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: lento is the musical direction meaning slowly

explanation.surface: Something crept forward but never arrived at its destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advanced' looks like moving forward, matching 'slowly', but it means advanced as a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance money is to lend it, so the past tense advanced matches the loaned sense.

clue.text: Hapless Frenchman's single talent is catching fish

parts.note: un is French for one

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a forte is a strong point or talent
tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: An unlucky Frenchman whose one gift is angling.
explanation.definitionFit: Hapless and unlucky are synonyms: someone without hap, or luck, is ill-fated.

clue.text: Excuse sailor on crack

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
to crack a puzzle is to solve it

explanation.surface: A seaman is let off for taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' reads as the drug, but it means solve, as with a code.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone is to pardon or free them from blame, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Adversaries chuck me into river upside down

indicators.note: in a down entry, upside down means the letters are read bottom to top
chuck, to throw, sends one piece into another
into marks where the thrown piece lands, inside the river

parts.note: the Seine is the river through Paris
taken as written

explanation.surface: Foes threaten to hurl the speaker headfirst into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck ... into' gives SEIMENE, which 'upside down' turns over, as befits a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Enemies and adversaries are synonyms: both are opponents or foes.

clue.text: Beastly female is after a man

indicators.note: is after means this piece comes after the a in the answer

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, a female beast

explanation.surface: A nasty woman is chasing a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' looks like nasty, but it means belonging to beasts: a dam is a mother animal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Adam is the first man, and the name comes from the Hebrew word for man or humankind.

clue.text: Actor named Ben gets into do-it-yourself (whisky production here)

indicators.note: gets into means the actor's surname is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: Ben Stiller is an American actor

explanation.surface: Ben Stiller takes up home improvement, apparently making whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A distillery is the works where spirits such as whisky are made.

clue.text: US film terminates unexpectedly

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals the letters of terminates are rearranged into a surprise order

explanation.surface: An American movie comes to an abrupt, surprising ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Main Street is the title of a 2010 American drama film, as well as the American name for a town's high street.

clue.text: Fellow's condition investigated after initial loss of temperature is revealed

parts.note: a fellow is a man; the 's is a link
if introduces a condition

indicators.note: initial loss means the letter goes from the front of the word

parts.note: to investigate something is to test it

explanation.surface: A man's illness, once tests are done and his fever drops, is disclosed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Condition' looks medical, but it is the word if.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifested means shown plainly or made evident, so it is a synonym of revealed.

clue.text: Wine imbibed during feast, invariably

indicators.note: imbibed during means the answer is swallowed within the following words

explanation.surface: Wine is always drunk at the banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont, an example of wine.

clue.text: With which wives punished husbands moving drunkenly on legs?

parts.note: a drunk lurching about is rolling
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: A cartoon wife waits with her weapon for a husband staggering home.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the comic-strip image of a wife waiting with a rolling pin for a drunken husband.
explanation.definitionFit: The rolling pin, a kitchen tool, is the traditional cartoon weapon of an angry wife.

clue.text: Dank fog rose out of place that's deserted

indicators.note: out of place means the letters of the dank fog phrase are displaced into a new order

explanation.surface: Damp mist rises from a bleak, abandoned spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of place' reads as the start of 'place that's deserted', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A godforsaken spot is dismal and desolate, so it suits deserted as a near synonym.

clue.text: Animal approaching net? Keep away

indicators.note: approaching means the animal comes up to, and just before, the next piece

parts.note: a steer is a young bullock
net and clear both mean after deductions, as in clear profit

explanation.surface: A beast is heading for a net, so stay out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Net' looks like a mesh, but it is an adjective meaning after deductions.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer clear is an idiom for avoiding something, staying out of its path.

clue.text: Slovenian leaders mediated after a fashion in Arab countries

indicators.note: after a fashion means in some manner, so the letters are made over in a new order

parts.note: the leaders, or first two letters, of Slovenian are S and L

explanation.surface: Slovenia's heads of government brokered peace, sort of, among Arab states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' is plural, so it supplies the first two letters, SL, which join MEDIATED in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The Middle East is the region of southwest Asia that includes most Arab nations.

clue.text: Passing through Turkey regularly, I save tax

indicators.note: passing through means these letters go inside the selected letters
regularly means every other letter of the country's name is taken

parts.note: save and but both mean except

explanation.surface: A traveller crossing Turkey hopes to avoid paying duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes T, R and E from Turkey; I and BUT go inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribute was a payment exacted by a ruler, a form of tax or levy.

clue.text: Craftsman not so happy to enlist learner

indicators.note: to enlist is to take in a recruit, so the learner goes inside

parts.note: sadder means less happy
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A miserable artisan reluctantly takes on an apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddler is a craftsman who makes saddles and other leather horse gear.

clue.text: Play darts, say, first taking aim

indicators.note: first means the aim piece is placed at the front of the answer

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim
darts is an example of a game

explanation.surface: Someone playing darts lines up the first throw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: Beckett's drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Endgame is a play by Samuel Beckett, so the name is an example of a stage drama.

clue.text: English officer, note, with a number of commendations

parts.note: NCO is a non-commissioned officer
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An English officer receives several commendations with a note.
explanation.definitionFit: Encomia is the plural of encomium, a formal speech or text of high praise.

clue.text: Absolutely right to sound horn on Calais thoroughfare

parts.note: to toot is to sound a horn
rue is the French for street, as in a town like Calais

explanation.surface: A driver honks on a French street and is quite right to do so.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom of rueful agreement, saying something is sadly correct.

clue.text: They work hard, taking about a month to tidy up

indicators.note: taking about means the reversed word goes round the month
in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to sort is to tidy
Jan is short for January

explanation.surface: Workers take about a month to clear up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns SORT into TROS, which holds JAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To work like a Trojan is an idiom for working very hard, so Trojans are hard workers.

clue.text: Whizz kid in classes always 'as everyone's attention

parts.note: CL is an abbreviation for class; the plural supplies it twice
ever means always
the second of the two class abbreviations
hogs everyone's attention with its H dropped, as the apostrophe in the clue signals

explanation.surface: A clever pupil always commands the room's attention in lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classes' gives CL twice. 'As is a dropped-H 'has', so the matching word HOGS also drops its H: 'OGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever clogs is a mocking British nickname for a know-all, a smart young person.

clue.text: Repeat left-wing orthodoxy at the outset

parts.note: red means left-wing or communist

indicators.note: at the outset means only the first letter of orthodoxy is used

explanation.surface: A socialist line is restated from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To redo something is to perform it again, which is to repeat it.

clue.text: Editor's comment put round end of manuscript

indicators.note: round means the verb's letters wrap around the following piece

parts.note: to set something is to put it

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of manuscript is used

explanation.surface: An editor scribbles a note at the foot of a typescript.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet, Latin for let it stand, is the proofreader's mark cancelling a correction.

clue.text: It was a mild oath 500 years back

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
an age is a long period of years

explanation.surface: A gentle curse that was current five centuries ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is an archaic exclamation, a minced form of by God used as a mild expletive.

clue.text: Financiers met, assembling outside Underground station

indicators.note: outside means the shuffled letters go around the financiers
assembling means the letters of met are put together in a new order

parts.note: bankmen are bankers or financiers

explanation.surface: Bankers gathered outside a London Tube stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' reads as a verb in the surface; 'assembling' makes EMT, which goes 'outside' the financiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Embankment is a station on the London Underground, beside the Thames.

clue.text: Outsiders in race coming round at speed

indicators.note: coming round means the two outer letters enclose the next word
the outsiders are the first and last letters of race

explanation.surface: Long shots in a race sweep round the bend at pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outsiders' sounds like long-odds horses, but it means the end letters R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Rate means pace or velocity, as in going at a fair rate.

clue.text: Successfully completing training, dance and celebrate loudly

parts.note: pas is a ballet step or dance
to sing out is to shout or proclaim joyfully

explanation.surface: Cadets finish their course, dance and cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: A passing-out parade marks cadets graduating from military training.
